context: a letter from W. E. Darwin, which you are answering
exchanges:
I send you pulmonaria anthers, I took them out of buds.

they gradually opened on the gum drying, and the Long styled marked xxx was quite open.

the one marked xx I saw was much larger than 3 of the others. So I took it off the glass after drawing and compared its pollen with long styled pollen, and there is no doubt that it is long styled. x I know also to be long styled, & I am pretty nearly sure that x & xx did not come from the same plant, by the help of drawing or rather making marks under camera lucida, & also counting with my eye & marking on paper; I have made a rough calculation of the comparative bad & good pollen in the long & short. of course it cannot be accurate, as in the case of little clusters of them I had partly to guess, also I dare say in some cases pollen tipped up on end or squashed may have mislead, but there is not the least doubt that there are many more imperfect in the long than in the short.

I took pollen from 2 plants of each kind. I found as follows

in Short styled out of 265 pollen grains

247 were good

18 — bad

Long styled out of 193 pollen grains

140 were good

53 — bad.

if you like, I will measure some more, if you think of any better way please tell me. I cannot judge wh. has most pollen.

I got Mamma’s letter about Menyanthes. I have written to the isle of Wight to find a station, & I am going off to Lyndhurst

Your affect son | W E Darwin

Yr observation on the 1 big anther with its differently sized pollen grains is a quite new & most extraordinary discovery. I remember distinctly seeing one anther much larger than all the others; but I never dreamed of the pollen-grains differing.

Never mind whether it kills you or not search more flowers & measure pollen & keep memorandum how many times you succeed for I shall lay great stress on this to me most unexpected discovery.

I return your letter (which keep most safely) & it may be of service to you, but more especially because I think you have written one, or 2 words wrong which I have pencilled for correction.

Never mind Menianthes Rhamnus or your life but work this out. Goodbye | what weather | C. D.

I wish you many ever get the little mare. She does beautifully—
